summary: Priority escalation during regional failover overrides explicit tenant model pin causing degraded routing and unexpected billing
description: Pulse Health reports that during a short region-level failover window an automated priority escalation (capacity-protection) bumped fallback routes and effectively superseded an explicit tenant pin to redwood/v1-chat-6B@2026-02-19. Requests were routed to open/llama-13b-quant and produced truncated answers and missing clinic identifiers. Customer saw a 37% increase in billed tokens for the window and open tickets from end-users. Pins should be authoritative; fallback routing should not revoke an explicit tenant pin.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant pins path /v1/generate to redwood/v1-chat-6B@2026-02-19 via tenant config and confirms active sessions
2) Trigger regional control-plane health degrade for us-east (internal test flag) to simulate failover conditions
3) Allow priority-escalation policy (configured for preemptive capacity protection) to run which increases fallback variant weight
4) Observe routing table and request traces: pinned tenant traffic is routed to fallback variant for ~22 minutes
5) Compare generation outputs and billing token counts during the window
investigation: Initial triage: Support validated customer pin exists and had a recent last-updated timestamp. Edge logs show a decision to route 100% of requests to fallback variant for tenant scope during 2026-03-10T03:14:00Z - 2026-03-10T03:36:00Z.

SRE findings: orchestrator emitted a priority escalation event tied to autoscale/spot-eviction signals in us-east; the routing policy evaluation path applied a higher-priority routing rule that did not check tenant-explicit pins in the fast-path.

Telemetry: trace IDs 5a9e... and 7f3b... show decision path short-circuited to fallback when control-plane responded with degraded capacity hints. Router version: v2.17.3. Route-manager commit: f1c2d3b. Edge-proxy v1.9.2 had recent config reloads at the same minute.

Hypothesis: priority-escalation policy was implemented in the global rule-set and uses a higher precedence rank than tenant pin rules in the current matching algorithm. During failover the rule ranked above tenant pins and caused transparent fallback.
Immediate risk: customers with pinned critical models may receive degraded models during automation windows; billing code path increments tokens for fallback model usage.

Next steps: reproduce in staging with same router/orchestrator versions, create safe policy change that ensures tenant-explicit pin checks are performed before priority escalation acceptance, and prepare rollback for policy change if it affects scale safety.

resolution: Workaround applied: Temporarily disabled automated priority escalation for tenant-scoped routes in us-east while fix validated. This prevented further pin overrides.

Fix in progress: routing matching engine patch to ensure tenant-explicit pins are evaluated before global priority-escalation rules. Patch referenced in PR github.com/redwood-inference/route-manager/pull/418.
Billing remediation: Billing Ops will calculate a token credit for Pulse Health for the 2026-03-10 window. Support will coordinate outbound communication.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add integration tests for precedence invariants; 2) Add explicit observability metric for 'pin-override' events; 3) Update runbook to require guard rails when enabling priority escalation in a region with pinned tenants; 4) Schedule audit of other global policies for precedence issues.
